explanations: terra: After the descent, whoever follows God's guidance has neither fear nor grief, casting guidance as the protection needed after leaving an earlier dwelling.

luna: The House is made مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا, a return and safety for people; the same ayah records God's covenant with Abraham and Ishmael to purify it. | terra: God makes the House a place of return and security, making explicit the section's claim that the guided route has a home and safe arrival.

luna: Abraham asks God to make the city secure and provide its people with fruits; it joins the section's safe destination with the herd and gift as provision. | terra: Abraham asks that this be a secure city and that its people receive fruits, combining safe settlement and provision near the House.

luna: After the House is declared a place of return and safety in 2:125, Abraham and Ishmael raise its foundations and ask God to accept their service; this adds the act of preparing the destination. | terra: Abraham and Ishmael raise the House's foundations and ask acceptance; this row supplies the constructed home immediately before their request to be shown the rites.
terra: Abraham and Ishmael ask to be shown their rites while raising the House's foundations; it supplies the rite-request surrounding the House of 2:125.
terra: In the qiblah dispute, God guides whom He wills to a straight path; orientation toward the House becomes a test of being directed.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to turn his face toward the Sacred Mosque, a concrete bodily direction toward the section's House.
terra: Wherever travelers emerge from, they are to turn toward the Sacred Mosque; this makes the House a direction carried through movement.
terra: The repeated qiblah command ends with completion of God's favor and the hope that people will be guided, linking direction, نعمة, and hidayah.

luna: This ayah calls Safa and Marwa signs of God and places them in Hajj and Umrah, making pilgrimage's marked route visible. | terra: Safa and Marwa are God's ritual signs, and their circuit belongs to Hajj or umrah; they broaden the section's marked pilgrimage landscape.
terra: Meat dedicated to other than God is prohibited, distinguishing true invocation over food or offering from rival dedication.
luna: The source section's dictionary calls the Hajj season a marker where people gather; this ayah says the new moons are appointed times for people and Hajj, a calendar marker for that gathering.

luna: The source section quotes this very rule: complete Hajj and Umrah, and do not release the pilgrim state until الهدي reaches its محل, its appointed place. | terra: Until the hady reaches its mahill directly supplies the section's animal, journey, and appointed arrival.

luna: The source section makes the Hajj season a marked time of gathering; this ayah calls Hajj's months known, giving the season a defined calendar place. | terra: Hajj has known months, giving Qur'anic substance to the section's season as a marked time of gathering.

luna: This Hajj passage names المشعر الحرام, the sacred landmark, and tells pilgrims to remember God there after leaving Arafat; it closely matches the section's season-as-marker and gathering. | terra: At the Hajj stations people remember God as He guided them after earlier error; rite, gathered place, remembrance, and hidayah converge.

luna: After the Arafat landmark in 2:198, this ayah tells pilgrims to depart from where the people depart and seek forgiveness, adding the movement of the gathered Hajj crowd. | terra: Pilgrims are told to depart from where the people depart and ask forgiveness; its own contribution is the shared movement of the Hajj assembly.

luna: This ayah says that after completing the rites pilgrims should remember God; it continues the Hajj season's gathering and links its marked days to the named remembrance developed in the section.
luna: In the same Hajj passage, this ayah gives the petition for good in this life and the Hereafter and protection from the Fire, a prayer for provision and a safe final destination.

luna: The Hajj passage returns to remembrance of God on numbered days; this gives the season's marker a fixed ritual calendar and continues the gathering beyond Arafat. | terra: Numbered days of remembrance close the Hajj instructions; this row contributes the calendared, communal finish to the pilgrimage scene.
terra: Divorced women are not to be prevented from marrying their husbands again when they agree honorably, a concrete reopening of the marital home.

luna: The section's path reaches a House; this ayah identifies the first House at Bakkah as blessed and guidance for all worlds. | terra: The first House is blessed and guidance for the worlds; House and huda stand together in a form especially close to the section's road ending at a home.

luna: The section describes the House as a destination and the refugee as protected; this ayah says whoever enters the House is safe and makes pilgrimage to it a duty. | terra: The House has clear signs, entrance into it is safety, and pilgrimage to it is a duty: destination, marker, sanctuary, and journey cohere.

luna: This ayah reports a demand for a قربان consumed by fire as proof from a messenger, together with a claimed covenant; unlike the section's devotional Hady, the offering is made a test for rejecting messengers.

luna: The section says the bride is led to her husband's household after marriage; this ayah orders that women's dowries be given as a gift, نِحْلَةً, in that marriage bond. | terra: Women are to receive their bridal gifts graciously; the gift branch is placed inside the bride-and-marriage branch rather than mere exchange.
terra: A husband who has given his wife even a great amount may not take it back, guarding the bridal gift after it has been given.

luna: The source section's dictionary branch for root ر ب ب names a covenant, and its bride is joined through marriage; this ayah calls marriage a مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا, a solemn covenant. | terra: Marriage is described as a solemn covenant, giving Qur'anic form to the section's bride being joined to a husband and the protecting word of covenant.
terra: A lexical bridge with a real limit: the section's m-l-k marriage sense meets the ayah's ownership sense, which it distinguishes from marriage sought with wealth and chastity.
terra: The verse permits marriage to believing women in an ownership context with their people's permission and bridal payments, bringing m-l-k, marriage, covenantal consent, and gift together.

luna: The source section asks اهدنا الصراط المستقيم; this ayah says God would guide people to a straight path, closely matching the plea's wording and action. | terra: God says He would guide the obedient to a straight path, retaining the request's path language as a destination-directed divine act.

luna: Following the straight-path promise in 4:68, this ayah identifies the companions as those God has favored, echoing the source phrase أنعمت عليهم in its human, not livestock, sense. | terra: Those who obey God and the Messenger are with the people upon whom God has bestowed favor; it expands the Fatiha's أنعمت into a gathered destination-community.

luna: This ayah protects people who join a community with a covenant or come offering peace; it says not to fight them if they withdraw, matching the section's shelter and safe-conduct image. | terra: People attached to a group with whom there is a treaty are exempt from attack when they withdraw from fighting, a legal shelter created by covenant.

luna: This ayah depicts people who remain in an oppressive land being asked why they did not migrate; it contrasts with the section's seeker who is led out to a safe place, while the following verses exempt those unable to leave.

luna: The ayah promises that whoever emigrates for God will find much refuge and abundance on earth, then speaks of death arriving on the road; it makes migration's shelter and destination explicit. | terra: One who emigrates for God finds many places of refuge and abundance, and even departure from home cut short by death remains a completed Godward journey.
terra: Fulfill contracts immediately precedes the prohibition on violating hady and House-bound pilgrims in 5:2; this row supplies the covenant principle.

luna: The source section says the offering and a person seeking protection are inviolable; this ayah forbids violating الهدي, the garlanded offerings, or those heading to the Sacred House. | terra: The verse makes hady, garlanded animals, and people heading for the Sacred House jointly inviolable, matching the section's protected offering and traveler.

luna: The section places God's name over its offering; this ayah forbids what was dedicated to other than God, stating the opposite boundary for an animal's consecration. | terra: Meat dedicated to other than God and slaughter on idolatrous altars are forbidden, marking the boundary around the section's God-named offering.

luna: This ayah permits game caught by trained hunting animals and commands ذكر اسم الله عليه; it parallels the section's tamed animal and the name that accompanies food. | terra: For trained hunting animals, God's name is mentioned over what they catch; the named-animal rule is extended beyond the Hajj offering.
terra: Remember God's favor and the covenant He bound with the believers joins the section's an'amta favor branch to its Rabb/covenant branch.

luna: The source section asks for guidance to a straight path that reaches a home; this ayah says God guides those seeking His pleasure to paths of peace and then to a straight path. | terra: Those following God's good pleasure are guided to paths of peace and brought from darkness into light, a plural-path form of the section's safe arrival.

luna: The section says the offering is قربى إلى الله; this ayah uses قربانا for the offering of Adam's two sons and distinguishes what God accepts from what He does not. | terra: The two sons of Adam each bring a qurban, and acceptance depends on God-consciousness; sacrifice is shown as an approach whose meaning exceeds the object.
terra: God tests pilgrims with game within reach of hands and spears; its own contribution is the animal-restraint test for which 5:95 then gives hady expiation.

luna: The source section's dictionary form الهدي is an offering; this ayah specifies an offering that reaches the Kaaba, الهديا بالغ الكعبة, in the rule for a hunting violation during pilgrimage. | terra: Its expiation is a hady reaching the Ka'bah, explicitly joining the offering to the House it must attain.
terra: Land game is forbidden while in consecrated pilgrimage even as sea game is allowed, distinguishing Hajj restraint from ordinary animal use.

luna: The section brings the sacrificial animal to a House and links it to the Hajj season; this ayah makes the Sacred Kaaba, sacred month, offerings, and garlands a standing for people. | terra: The Ka'bah, sacred months, hady, and garlands are made a support for people; it gathers the House, seasonal marker, offering, and public assembly.

luna: The section's Hady is a divinely named offering; this ayah rejects self-invented livestock taboos such as bahira and saiba, marking a boundary between prescribed offering and invented animal sanctity. | terra: God has not instituted the pagan animal designations bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah, and ham; fabricated consecrations contrast with His appointed hady.
luna: The disciples ask Jesus whether his Lord can send down a table from heaven; this is a specific offered-table scene parallel to the section's dictionary sense of a gift carried on a platter.
luna: The disciples say they want to eat from the table and have their hearts reassured; this states the recipients' need within the table-gift scene begun in 5:112.
luna: Jesus asks God to send a table from heaven as a feast and sign and asks Him to provide for them; it develops the section's secondary tray-and-gift image as a divine provision.
luna: God says He will send the table, then warns of severe punishment for disbelief afterward; this completes the gift scene with the boundary attached to refusing its sign.
terra: After God has guided us, should we be turned back like one lured bewildered while companions call him toward guidance? It dramatizes loss and recall of a route.
terra: Those whose faith is not mixed with wrongdoing have security and are rightly guided, directly pairing the section's safe arrival with hidayah.
luna: This ayah says God made the stars so people may find their way through the darkness of land and sea, a concrete navigation scene for the section's dictionary sense of showing someone a road.

luna: The section says God's name is spoken over the sacrificial animal; this ayah permits eating what has had God's name mentioned over it. | terra: The command to eat what God's name was mentioned over directly realizes the section's named animal at the meal.

luna: After 6:118 permits food over which God's name was mentioned, this ayah asks why people would not eat it and states the exception for compulsion; it continues the named-food rule in its own context. | terra: It asks why believers should not eat that over which God's name has been mentioned, clarifying the positive command in 6:118.

luna: Where 6:118 permits food over which God's name was mentioned, this ayah forbids eating what lacks that mention; it marks the boundary around the section's named offering. | terra: Do not eat what God's name has not been mentioned over; it states the negative boundary of the named-animal practice in 6:118.
terra: The verse calls this the straight path of the Lord; the next ayah supplies its safe dwelling, so this row establishes the route itself.
terra: Those who heed the path have an Abode of Peace with their Lord, who is their protector; 6:126 supplies the straight-path neighbor.

luna: This ayah describes people assigning portions of crops and livestock to God and partners, then misdirecting those portions; it reverses the section's animal sincerely offered as قربى to God. | terra: People assign shares of crops and cattle to God and to partners, then manipulate them; this corrupts the offering's Godward purpose.
terra: Invented livestock prohibitions include animals over which God's name is not pronounced, a direct reversal of the section's named sacrifice.

luna: The source section's herd word is الأنعام; this ayah divides livestock into burden-bearing and other kinds, then calls it God's provision to eat, showing the same animals as transport and food. | terra: Among cattle are animals for carrying burdens and for food; this supplies the serviceable herd beneath the section's sacrificial camel.
terra: The livestock polemic explicitly names the camel pair and cattle pair, making the section's an'am-camel identification concrete within Qur'anic animal law.
terra: The dietary prohibition includes what was dedicated to other than God, repeating the naming boundary in a legal list.

luna: The source section's root ه د ي appears here in هداني ربي إلى صراط مستقيم; the ayah names Abraham's upright way as the destination of God's guidance. | terra: The Prophet says his Lord has guided him to a straight path, an upright religion of Abraham; guidance is inseparable from a lived way of worship.

luna: Immediately after the guided path in 6:161, Abraham says his prayer and sacrifice, life and death are for God; this directly joins the section's worship with its offering. | terra: Prayer and sacrifice alike belong wholly to God; it makes the offering's purpose the nearness and devotion emphasized in the section.
terra: People admitted to the Garden say God guided them to this; the utterance names a completed destination rather than guidance as abstraction.

luna: The section protects the Hady and those headed to the House; Salih's she-camel is declared a sign and must be left unharmed, another camel whose sacred status forbids interference. | terra: God's she-camel is a sign and must not be harmed; its protected status parallels the inviolable animal in the House-bound offering scene.
terra: Thamud hamstrings the she-camel after the prohibition, a reversal of the care owed to a divinely protected animal.
luna: The source section draws النعم from the same root family as أنعمت; this ayah calls heedless people like cattle, even more astray, reversing the blessed and guided people of the image.

luna: The section's dictionary says a bride is gathered to her husband and joined to him; this ayah says a spouse is made so he may find rest with her, لِيَسْكُنَ إِلَيْهَا. | terra: A mate is made from the one soul so that he may find tranquility with her, giving the bride branch a form of settled attachment.
terra: When believers were few and feared being snatched away, God gave them shelter, aid, and good provision; asylum, safety, and provision are explicit together.
terra: Those who bar access to the Sacred Mosque are denied true guardianship of it; the verse clarifies that protection of the House belongs with the reverent, not obstructers.

luna: Believers who gave emigrants shelter and support are named as allies; this is a community receiving people who have left home, parallel to the section's protected arrival. | terra: Those who gave the emigrants shelter and help are bound by mutual responsibility, while a treaty limits intervention; refuge and covenant occur together.

luna: Following the shelter and support described in 8:72, this ayah again joins emigrants with those who give them refuge and promises forgiveness and honorable provision to them. | terra: The emigrants and those who sheltered and helped them are affirmed together; it confirms the refuge relationship detailed in 8:72.

luna: The section's season is a marker where people gather; this ayah has a public announcement to people on the day of the greater Hajj. | terra: A public proclamation is made on the day of the greater pilgrimage, giving the section's Hajj gathering its covenantal public setting.

luna: The source section's dictionary branch for ر ب ب explains protection through covenant; this ayah orders treaties with those who have kept faith to be honored until their agreed term. | terra: Treaties with partners who have not violated them are to be honored to their term, supplying the reliable word that the section says protects a seeker.

luna: This ayah directly stages the section's protected stranger: if a polytheist asks for refuge, protect him, let him hear God's word, then deliver him to his safe place, مَأْمَنَهُ. | terra: One who seeks protection is sheltered until hearing God's word and then delivered to his مأمن; it is the section's asylum-seeker brought to safety.

luna: Following the asylum rule in 9:6, this ayah speaks of treaties at the Sacred Mosque and commands fairness while the other party keeps its terms, linking protection to a kept covenant. | terra: The treaty made near the Sacred Mosque is to be upheld while the other party upholds it, tying covenantal protection to the House's precinct.
terra: Giving water to pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque are named as House-related services, giving the gathering a human custodial scene.

luna: This ayah bars polytheists from approaching the Sacred Mosque after that year, setting a limit on access to the sanctuary beside 9:6's temporary protection and safe escort for a polytheist seeking refuge. | terra: After their appointed year, polytheists are barred from the Sacred Mosque; this is a boundary around the protected House and its pilgrimage space.
luna: This ayah sets the year at twelve months with four sacred months, a calendar boundary for the section's marked Hajj season and inviolable offerings.
luna: This ayah condemns moving the sacred months from their appointed places; it marks the boundary against shifting the season that the section treats as a sign for gathering.

luna: The section's refugee seeks a safe place in order to be protected; this ayah says hypocrites would rush to any refuge, cave, or hiding place to evade obligation, a morally opposite use of shelter. | terra: If hypocrites could find a refuge, cave, or place of entry, they would rush toward it; flight into shelter is contrasted with the honored asylum of 9:6.
terra: The three who lagged behind learn that there is no refuge from God except with Him, relocating all secure arrival to the divine side.

luna: This ayah says the Lord guides believers by their faith and has rivers flow beneath them in gardens, a direct progression from guidance to a destination of repose. | terra: Faith guides believers toward gardens beneath which rivers run, pairing hidayah with an inhabited final place.

luna: This ayah joins the section's two images in one sentence: God invites people to دار السلام and guides whom He wills to a straight path. | terra: God calls to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path, making the path-to-home relation explicit.
terra: The question contrasts one who guides to truth with one needing guidance, clarifying the guide-led relation behind ihdina.
terra: Noah's son seeks a mountain to protect him from the flood, but Noah says none protects from God's command except those granted mercy; a false safe place fails.

luna: Salih calls his she-camel a sign and commands his people to leave her grazing in God's land without harm; this parallels the section's protected offering animal. | terra: The she-camel is God's sign and is to graze unharmed; the repeated scene reinforces animal inviolability outside the Hajj rite.

luna: The people hamstring Salih's protected she-camel, the direct reversal of the section's inviolable Hady; the following warning makes the consequence of violating that boundary explicit. | terra: After killing the she-camel, Thamud are given only three days; violating the protected sign has the opposite outcome to honoring God's symbols.
terra: Every people has a guide, giving the section's request for guidance a human-prophetic counterpart.
luna: This ayah places the righteous with their spouses and families in gardens they enter through the gates, joining the section's bride-and-house image to a final home.
luna: The next ayah gives the angels' greeting of peace to those entering the Garden; it completes the household-arrival scene in 13:23 with a safe welcome.
terra: God guides to Himself whoever turns back to Him, giving guidance an explicitly Godward destination.
terra: Those who believe have goodness and a beautiful homecoming; in the surrounding guidance passage, the end of turning to God is named as return.
terra: The Book brings people from darkness to light by their Lord's permission, toward the path of the Mighty and Praiseworthy.
terra: The messengers say God has guided them to their ways; their trust turns received guidance into a route they can inhabit.
terra: Abraham asks that the city be made secure, grounding the section's inviolable House and safe destination in a prayer for sanctuary.

luna: Abraham settles his family by the Sacred House so they can establish prayer, asks that people's hearts incline toward them, and asks for provision; this joins home, worship, and being drawn toward the House. | terra: Abraham settles his offspring in the barren valley beside God's Sacred House, asking that hearts incline there and that they receive provision.

luna: The source section identifies النعم as camels and livestock; this ayah says God created cattle for warmth, benefits, and food, making the herd from which the Hady is drawn visible as provision. | terra: Cattle provide warmth, benefits, and food, making the herd a received provision before it becomes an offering.

luna: The adjoining ayah describes the herd as beautiful when brought home in the evening and driven out in the morning; it gives an everyday return-and-departure scene behind the animal led away to the House.

luna: This ayah shows livestock carrying people's burdens to distant land; the section reverses that direction, with the camel itself led on a journey to its sacred destination. | terra: The animals carry burdens to a land people could scarcely reach themselves, a travel-and-arrival role close to the section's carried homeward animal.

luna: The source section's root ه د ي includes showing a road and bringing someone to a house; this ayah says God laid roads in the earth so people may be guided along them. | terra: Mountains, rivers, and roads are set in the earth so people may be guided; 16:16 then identifies landmarks and stars for that movement.

luna: The source section develops ma'lam as a marker where people gather and connects it to hidaya; this ayah pairs landmarks, علامات, with being guided by the stars. | terra: God sets landmarks and stars by which travelers are guided. The section explicitly links its wasam/ma'lam observation to marks that orient a route.
terra: Those who emigrate after being wronged are promised a good settlement in this world, a divine answer to departure from home.
terra: God makes spouses, children, and good provision; it connects the bride branch to household formation and sustenance.
terra: From cattle skins God makes houses and portable shelters, an unusual direct meeting of herd, travel, and home.
luna: The source section's dictionary branch for ر ب ب treats a bond as an عهد and ميثاق; this ayah commands people to fulfill God's covenant and not break oaths after confirming them.

luna: The section's destination offers protection and provision; this ayah pictures a secure, provisioned town losing both after ingratitude, a reversal of shelter as a gift. | terra: A town once safe, tranquil, and supplied from every place tastes hunger and fear after ingratitude, the contrary outcome to the House's provision and security.
terra: The same exclusion of what was dedicated to other than God places the named-animal rule within God's provision and necessity allowance.
luna: The section glosses worship as obedience; Abraham is described here as قانتا لله, devotedly obedient to God, in the same Abrahamic setting as pilgrimage and offering.
luna: The source section links root ن ع م in أنعمت to livestock; this ayah uses the same favor-family for Abraham, then says God chose and guided him to a straight path.
terra: The Qur'an guides to what is most upright, making the section's requested route a scriptural direction rather than a bare line.
luna: The source section's dictionary branch for root ر ب ب describes a bond as covenant; this ayah commands people to fulfill their covenant and says they will be questioned about it.
terra: The prayer asks for a truthful entrance and a truthful exit with supporting authority, a compact invocation for rightly conducted departure and arrival.
luna: The youths take refuge in the cave and ask their Lord for mercy and a rightly ordered outcome; this is another explicit request for shelter and guidance from within it.
terra: The cave youths believe in their Lord and are increased in guidance; this supplies the inner hidayah of the refuge scene continued in 18:16-17.

luna: After the youths withdraw from their people, this ayah tells them to take refuge in the cave and promises mercy and a prepared outcome, completing the shelter scene of 18:10. | terra: The companions are told to take refuge in the cave, where their Lord will spread mercy and prepare their affair; physical shelter becomes divinely given safety.
terra: The cave's opening is described in a protected physical scene, and the verse declares that the one God guides is truly guided; refuge and hidayah overlap.
terra: No one can alter God's words, and none can find a refuge apart from Him; this supplies the ultimate limit on human protection.
terra: Abraham asks his father to follow him so he can guide him to an even path, a personal guide inviting another into a sound route.
terra: Moses describes the Lord as giving every thing its created form and then guiding it, matching the section's interest in what is made fit and led.
terra: After humanity's descent, divine guidance is promised; following it prevents both going astray and misery, a direct boundary for the homeward path.
terra: The ending asks who are the companions of the even path and who has been guided, making right arrival a disclosed distinction.

luna: This ayah says the Sacred Mosque is for resident and visitor alike and warns against hindering access; it gives a boundary around the House to which the section's offering and pilgrim are headed. | terra: The Sacred Mosque is for resident and visitor alike, while intending violation there brings warning; it frames the House as a guarded shared destination.

luna: The section's animal is taken to the House as قربى and serves worship; here Abraham is told to purify God's House for those who circle it, stand, bow, and prostrate. | terra: God assigns Abraham the place of the House and tells him to cleanse it for those who circle, stand, bow, and prostrate; this gives the destination its worshipful origin.

luna: The section's guidance image has a road ending at a House; this ayah calls people to Hajj and pictures them arriving on foot and on lean camels from distant passes. | terra: Abraham is told to proclaim pilgrimage, and people come by every distant route, giving the section's movement toward the House its gathered, public scene.

luna: The section's source root س م و concerns the name raised over the offered animal, and its root ن ع م names the herd; this ayah joins God's name, livestock He provided, appointed days, eating, and feeding the poor. | terra: Pilgrims witness benefits and remember God's name on provided cattle on known days; this extends the named-animal scene of 22:34 and 22:36.

luna: Following the Hajj call and offerings in 22:27-28, this ayah completes the approach with vows and circumambulation of the Ancient House; it supplies the arriving pilgrim's destination and rite. | terra: After the cattle rites, pilgrims complete their rites and circumambulate the Ancient House; its own contribution is the arrival-act at the section's destination.

luna: The section makes the Hady sacred and protected; this ayah says to honor God's sanctities and distinguishes lawful livestock from what has been recited as forbidden. | terra: Honoring God's sanctities is joined here to the lawfulness of livestock except stated restrictions; it extends the House passage's sacred boundary around the section's herd.

luna: The section treats the Hady as inviolable; this ayah says honoring God's sha'a'ir is from the piety of hearts, giving the animal's protected status a devotional meaning. | terra: Honoring God's ritual signs is piety of the hearts, furnishing the inward meaning of the marked sacrificial animals in the following scene.

luna: The source section's dictionary word الهدي is a sacrificial animal led to its appointed place; this ayah says its destination is the Ancient House, البيت العتيق. | terra: The section's dictionary sense of هدي is made spatial here: sacrificial animals have a fixed term, then their mahill is at the Ancient House.

luna: The source section links أنعمت to the herd word الأنعام through root ن ع م; this ayah names livestock as God's provision and commands that His name be remembered over them. | terra: Each community's rite includes remembering God's name over the cattle He provided, joining the section's an'am, sacrifice, and named worship.

luna: After 22:34 names God over livestock, this ayah describes the response when God is mentioned: hearts tremble, and the people pray, endure, and give. Its contribution is the worshipper's stance beside the offering rite.

luna: The source section's root س م و explains اسم as a name that raises the named one's remembrance; here God's name is recited over the standing sacrificial camels, which are then slaughtered and shared as food. | terra: The sacrificial camels are among God's ritual signs; His name is pronounced over them, and their meat is shared after sacrifice.

luna: The source section's dictionary form البعير المعبد means a subdued camel; this ayah says God subdued the sacrificial animals so people would magnify Him for the guidance He gave them. It brings the animal's submission, worship, and هدى together. | terra: God subjects the animals so people magnify Him for having guided them, exactly joining the tamed animal, worship, and hidayah in the section.
terra: Believers' hearts become humble before the revealed truth, and God guides them to a straight path; worshipful receptivity is its route.
terra: Those who emigrate and are killed or die will receive good provision and be admitted by an entrance they approve, joining provision to a welcomed arrival.
luna: This ayah assigns every community a rite so its people mention God's name over livestock He provided, then tells them to submit to the one God; it directly joins herd, offering, and service.
luna: The source section connects protection with عهد and ميثاق; this ayah identifies believers by their care for trusts and covenants, the reliability that makes a refuge promise meaningful.
terra: Noah asks, "My Lord, cause me to land at a blessed landing-place"; it is a direct prayer to be brought safely into a dwelling after travel.
terra: God protects while none can be protected against Him, making the efficacy of every asylum depend on the true Protector.
terra: The unmarried are to be married, and God may enrich them from His bounty; marriage is treated as a gathered household rather than private possession.

luna: The source section's root س م و describes the raised remembrance carried by a name; this ayah joins houses raised by God's leave with His name being remembered in them. | terra: In houses God has permitted to be raised, His name is remembered and He is glorified; it gives a House, elevated mention, and worship parallel.
terra: God promises to establish believers in the land and exchange their fear for security, the social scale of the section's safe place.

luna: The source section links the livestock word الأنعام to أنعمت; here people who do not listen or reason are compared to cattle and called more astray in the way, a pointed reversal of the requested guidance.
terra: At the sea Moses says his Lord is with him and will guide him; guidance appears at a threatened crossing toward safety.
terra: Abraham names God as the One who created him and then guides him, pairing originating creation with ongoing direction.
terra: The she-camel has an allotted drinking turn beside the people's turn, presenting an animal with a protected, regulated claim.

luna: The queen's warning that kings corrupt cities and humble their honored people frames why she sends the gift in 27:35; this verse contributes the political danger behind that failed offering. | terra: The queen's fear that kings ruin towns explains why the gift of 27:35 is diplomatic rather than the section's gift to a beloved friend.

luna: The source section's dictionary form الهدية is a gift sent to someone; here the Queen says she will send a هدِيَّة to Solomon and wait for the envoys' return. | terra: The queen sends a هدية to Solomon, the Qur'an's direct instance of the section's secondary h-d-y sense of a gift carried to another.

luna: Solomon rejects the Queen's هديتكم and says they rejoice in their gift; unlike the section's gift to a beloved recipient, this gift to a rival does not reach its intended home. | terra: Solomon rejects the gift and turns its value back on its senders, reversing the section's friendly gift that reaches its proper recipient.

luna: After rejecting the gift in 27:36, Solomon orders the envoys returned; this confirms that the gift is sent back and the road to its recipient is closed. | terra: Solomon orders the envoy to return; after 27:36 refuses the gift, this row turns the intended approach into an opposed return.
terra: God guides travelers through the darknesses of land and sea, a literal navigation scene for the section's road-and-arrival sense of h-d-y.

luna: The source section's root ه د ي includes showing a road and bringing someone to a house; as Moses travels toward Midian, he says, عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل, asking for guidance along the way. | terra: As Moses turns toward Midian, he asks that his Lord guide him to the sound way; this is a traveler seeking a real destination.

luna: Moses reaches the water of Midian, where shepherds water their flocks and two women hold theirs back; this supplies the herd, herdsmen, and roadside meeting that the section's gift, bride, and refuge images can meet.
luna: Moses waters the women's flock, then turns to shade and asks his Lord for whatever good He sends; the verse joins care for a herd to a request for provision and hospitality.
luna: One of the women comes to Moses and brings him toward her father's household, offering a reward for watering the flock; this meets the section's led-to-a-home and gift-for-kindness images.
luna: After the invitation in 28:25, the woman describes Moses as strong and trustworthy; this is the household's stated reason for receiving him and considering him for the marriage that follows.

luna: The section says the bride is led to her husband's home after nikah; here the father proposes marriage to one daughter on an agreed term of service, explicitly joining marriage and a binding arrangement. | terra: The father of Midian offers one daughter in marriage to Moses on a term of service, a narrated act of joining a bride to a husband.

luna: Moses accepts the marriage term and says God is witness to their agreement; this completes 28:27 and meets the section's covenant as the bond that secures a person received into a household. | terra: Moses accepts the marriage term and asks God to witness it; this row supplies the binding completion of the proposal in 28:27.
terra: The Prophet cannot guide whom he loves, while God guides whom He wills; it identifies the divine agent addressed by ihdina.
terra: The objection to following guidance is answered with God's secure sanctuary, to which fruits are brought; huda, refuge, and provision are explicit together.

luna: This ayah says God made the sanctuary secure while people around it were being seized; it clarifies the House's protective boundary that the section extends to a person seeking refuge. | terra: God has made a secure sanctuary while people around it are snatched away, sharpening the House as a protected place.
terra: Those who strive for God are guided to His ways, retaining the image of plural routes that lead toward the One sought.

luna: The section's gift is offered to one with mawadda; this ayah says God placed affection and mercy between spouses, giving the bride's household a relationship of affection. | terra: Spouses are made so that people find tranquility in them, giving the section's bride brought home an inward form of settled belonging.
terra: God says that He married Zaynab to Muhammad, a direct Qur'anic instance of a woman being joined to her husband by a decisive act.
terra: God places linked towns on a measured route and commands travel through them safely by night and day, a concrete scene of protected movement between dwellings.
terra: They ask for their journey-stages to be lengthened and wrong themselves, after which they are dispersed; it reverses the safe, measured route of 34:18.
terra: God's covenant with Adam's children forbids worship of Satan; this supplies the covenantal boundary for the straight worship-path in 36:61.
terra: Worship Me; this is a straight path directly binds the section's عبادة strand to the path it asks to be shown.
terra: Satan has led many astray after the command to worship God on the straight path, the route's active contrary pull.

luna: The source section uses root م ل ك for marriage; here فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ uses its ownership sense for livestock, making explicit that the herd from which an offering is taken is also held by people. | terra: God creates cattle for people and makes them theirs; the following ayat specify the tractable service central to the section's tamed animal.

luna: The source section's dictionary form البعير المعبد means a tamed camel; this ayah says God ذللناها, subdued livestock for people to ride and eat, a close parallel in sense. | terra: God makes cattle tractable, so some are mounts and some are eaten; this is a close Qur'anic parallel to the section's uysallaştırılmış camel.
terra: Cattle provide benefits and drinks, completing the provision side of the herd that is later offered and shared.
terra: The condemned are told to be led to the path of Hell, a severe reversal in which guidance-language carries people to the wrong final abode.
terra: Abraham's vision of sacrificing his son makes surrender and obedience the inner test behind a sacrificial scene.

luna: This ayah says Abraham's son was ransomed with a great sacrifice, a distinct sacrificial scene that shows an animal offering taking another's place in Abraham's story. | terra: The son is ransomed with a great sacrifice, making deliverance and offering meet.
terra: Moses and Aaron are guided to the straight path, a prophetic recurrence of the route requested in the section.

luna: The section's stated purpose is قربى to God through an offering; this ayah reports the rejected claim that worshipping other protectors will bring people nearer to God, exposing a rival route to nearness.
terra: The ayah places the making of spouses from one soul beside the eight pairs of cattle, a rare Qur'anic meeting of the section's bride and herd branches.
luna: This ayah describes the God-fearing being led in groups until they arrive at the Garden and its gates open, a clear scene of a guided road reaching a home.
luna: After arrival in 39:73, the Garden's people praise God for fulfilling His promise and giving them the land as inheritance; it supplies the welcomed residents' account of reaching their home.
terra: The believing man tells his people to follow him and he will guide them to the way of rectitude, echoing the guide-to-path relation.
terra: God creates cattle so that people may ride some and eat some, repeating the controlled animal's double use as mount and food.
terra: Cattle carry people's needs and their riders alongside ships, making them vehicles toward human purposes and destinations.
terra: Thamud are shown guidance but prefer blindness over it, a stated refusal of the path's offered direction.
terra: God makes spouses from people and pairs from cattle, again holding marriage and herd together in one generative scene.
terra: The revealed spirit is made a light through which God guides whom He wills to a straight path, linking the path to heard divine speech.
terra: God spreads out the earth and makes paths in it so people may be guided, a literal terrain-and-route counterpart to the section's way home.
terra: God makes ships and cattle for riding, preparing the concrete mount-and-journey scene developed in 43:13.

luna: The section describes a subdued camel set on a journey; this riding prayer says to remember the Lord's favor and glorify the One who subjected the mount. | terra: Upon mounting what God has subjected, travelers remember His favor and declare His transcendence; the verse makes riding a tamed creature an act of praise.

luna: The riding prayer begun in 43:13 ends here with إنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون, naming the journey's return to the Lord; it echoes the section's claim that a road has a destination. | terra: After the mount-and-praise of 43:13, the travelers confess that they will return to their Lord, adding the ultimate homeward horizon.
terra: Jesus says to worship God, his Lord and theirs; this is a straight path, repeating the worship-and-route conjunction.
luna: The section's قربى is directed to God; this ayah calls the false gods taken as قربانا useless when their worshippers need help, reversing the promised nearness.
terra: The jinn say the revealed Book guides to truth and to a straight path, making heard scripture a guide for travelers.

luna: The source section asks for guidance to a destination; following the account of those killed in God's cause, this ayah says God will guide them and set their condition right. | terra: God will guide the slain in His way and set their condition right; the following ayah gives the destination this guidance opens.

luna: The next ayah completes 47:5 by saying God will admit them to the Paradise He has made known to them, giving guidance a home at its end. | terra: God admits them to the Garden He has made known to them; this row supplies the recognized dwelling reached after the guidance of 47:5.
luna: The source section's herd animal is provision brought in worship; this ayah contrasts believers' promised Garden with disbelievers who eat like cattle and have the Fire as their abode.
terra: In the Hudaibiyah passage God promises to guide the Prophet to a straight path; 48:25 and 48:27 give that promise a House-and-pilgrimage setting.

luna: The section's الهدي is meant to reach its محل; here the offerings are held back from reaching that place while the believers are barred from the Sacred Mosque, a direct interruption of both arrivals. | terra: The hady is held back from its mahill while pilgrims are barred from the Sacred Mosque: the section's homeward movement is deliberately interrupted.

luna: After the offerings are held back in 48:25, this ayah promises entry into the Sacred Mosque safely and without fear, completing the interrupted road to the House. | terra: The believers will enter the Sacred Mosque in security and without fear, resolving the interruption of hady and pilgrimage in 48:25.
terra: In the Hudaibiyah passage, God sends His Messenger with guidance and true religion; it gives the surrounding House-and-pilgrimage episode its guiding mission.
terra: The believers' visible mark is on their faces from prostration; in the same Hudaibiyah-House setting, worship itself yields a recognisable sign.
terra: Guidance to faith is named as God's favor, directly illuminating the section's lexical meeting of an'amta and ihdina.
terra: The sending of the she-camel is a test, making this exceptional animal a divinely charged sign rather than mere livestock.
terra: Water is divided between the people and the she-camel; the verse gives the animal a publicly observed right within the community.
terra: Those who trusted their fortresses to protect them from God are reached from where they did not expect; fortified dwelling is not guaranteed sanctuary.

luna: This ayah describes emigrants driven from their homes and property who seek God's bounty and pleasure; it supplies the displaced travel behind the section's seeker of protection. | terra: The emigrants have been driven from their homes and possessions while seeking God's favor; it supplies the vulnerability answered by 59:9's welcome.

luna: The next ayah describes the people settled in the abode and faith who love those migrating to them and prefer them; it shows the welcoming household that completes 59:8. | terra: Those already settled in the home and faith love the emigrants and make room for them, a communal counterpart to the protected person received by a people.

luna: Believing women arrive as emigrants and must not be returned to disbelievers; the ayah then permits marriage to them with their dowries, joining refuge, a new household, and the bride's transfer. | terra: Believing women arrive as emigrants, are not returned to unbelievers, and may enter new marriages after bridal payments; asylum, bride, and gift meet in one legal scene.

luna: Pharaoh's wife asks her Lord to build her a house near Him in Paradise and save her from Pharaoh and wrongdoing people; it joins a woman's household, refuge, and final safe home. | terra: Pharaoh's wife asks for a house near God in Paradise and rescue from oppression, joining desired dwelling and refuge in one prayer.
terra: The ayah compares one moving face-down with one walking upright on a straight path, a bodily reversal that makes guided travel perceptible.

luna: The source section's root و س م includes marking or branding and uses the Hajj season as a landmark; this ayah uses its concrete branding sense on a person's snout, a harsh mark unlike a marker that gathers people. | terra: We shall brand him on the snout uses the section's w-s-m stamp branch as a punitive mark, reversing the communal marker of the pilgrimage season.
terra: The jinn call the Qur'an a recitation that guides to right conduct, a listener's response close to the protected seeker hearing God's word in 9:6.
terra: Humans seeking refuge with jinn only increase their burden; it is a contrary version of seeking protection from a people.
terra: The messenger says none can protect him from God and he will find no refuge besides Him, setting the boundary for every shelter.
terra: God has shown the human the way, whether grateful or ungrateful; the verse makes the path a responsible response to provision.
luna: The source section says the name raises the named one's remembrance; this command explicitly says سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى, joining the name to glorification and exaltation.
terra: The Creator proportioned, determined, and then guided, a compressed account of fitting and directing that illuminates the section's tamed, destined creature.

luna: The section's dictionary says the Hady may be a camel; this ayah specifically turns attention to camels and how they were created, keeping the actual animal in view beyond its ritual role. | terra: This is an object-level parallel: the section identifies the hady's animal as a camel, while this ayah calls for reflection on how the camel was created rather than on sacrifice.
terra: God shows the two elevated ways, presenting a visible choice of routes rather than an undifferentiated journey.

luna: This ayah identifies Salih's camel as God's and names her watering turn; it adds another protected camel scene beside the section's inviolable Hady. | terra: The messenger warns about God's she-camel and its watering, keeping the animal's protected status at the center of the warning.

luna: The people hamstring the she-camel in 91:13 and their Lord destroys them for it, a direct violation of the protected animal's boundary. | terra: They deny and hamstring the she-camel, so the town is leveled; it is the destructive opposite of honoring a protected animal.
terra: God declares that guidance rests with Him, reinforcing why the section's request is addressed to God.
terra: God found the Prophet searching and guided him, a speaker-centered memory of being brought from lack of direction.
terra: We raised your remembrance is the direct Qur'anic counterpart to the section's s-m-w claim that a name raises the mention of the one named.

luna: This command names the Lord of this House as the one to worship, directly meeting the section's link between the House, service, and devotion. | terra: The command is to worship the Lord of this House, coupling the home itself to the section's عبادة strand.

luna: The same passage says the Lord fed the people against hunger and made them safe from fear; it gives food and sanctuary safety as gifts of the House's Lord. | terra: The Lord of the House feeds people after hunger and secures them from fear, completing the section's provision and refuge motifs.

luna: On the sacrificial reading of وَانْحَرْ, this command pairs prayer with an offering directed to your Lord, matching the section's animal brought near through worship. | terra: The command to pray to the Lord and sacrifice binds sacrificial action directly to worship.
terra: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak. The section's asylum-seeker and its Rabb branch meet in a direct formula of refuge.
terra: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of people, another direct rendering of the protected seeker turning to a Rabb.
terra: The protector invoked in 114:1 is named King of people, bringing the Malik root's sovereign sense into the refuge formula.
